document.title: Colorado Academic Standards: Reading, Writing and Communicating

2116D875450F4AEB828236C88372F2E2.description: By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

2162B86E06FD4A1D9515D65C6EA5692C.description: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

21B87321F9AE4506B1458F93ADE0EC09.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

28AC6E8A720749EAB47B7D1A8F88E58B.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

2C8060D0659F441096777FA9111C90DB.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic.

319AF7874E56450E9A5F8237BA3AFE94.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9–10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

32B326F6949B491A9E04186BBAADF388.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

34A3DCAEA1D6405BBABE834529830905.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (for example: MLA Handbook, or APA handbook) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

3519A78B96D84FBE8DD042A400950541.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

35E236E091B54DCAA2884C2D387F6281.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

390C0E9569274B3CBEAF611A610654A9.description: Synthesize multiple, authoritative literary and/or informational sources, creating cohesive research projects that show an understanding of the subject.

393231AB09F8429C8B81C23F0C73C1F7.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (for example: visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

3B32611AB9174A9C9C495767ACE7B7CA.description: Write well-developed, unbiased arguments that are supported by substantive, valid reasoning and evidence.

3FBE33D0132C4152B10D3C8524D86A85.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

4012EA8E97184545A451100154289862.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.

425562322E7D4F59B88E8B433D95CEFD.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

42664B1FC1794EAA8FE786DEF293E7CC.description: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how an author uses rhetoric to advance that point of view or purpose.

42DF2C113B8D4FC2BDDAD7953B3BEC34.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (for example, articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

4EE21CF4FCBE497488871566A426AF13.description: Analyze various accounts of a subject told in different mediums (for example: a person's life story in both print and multimedia), determining which details are emphasized in each account.

500B5C60F6F246E9891AB1CC31EA8341.description: Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence, and between claim(s) and counterclaims.

50842E884A1D4F3AAD8FE94E6AD23D7D.description: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text (for example: a section or chapter).

51AFA47D0B7B411E879F760DF6513256.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings; analyze the cumulative impact of specific word choices on meaning and tone (for example: how the language of a court opinion differs from that of a newspaper).

54E04C60C5B24C2E9CCA646057FE490D.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (for example: informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

57385ED9911A4A5BBFCAF605A4925690.description: Correctly spell frequently used words and consult reference materials (for example: dictionaries, both print and digital, spell check, and/or trusted peers and/or adults) to determine the spelling of less frequent vocabulary.

5CAED67C308A4A0EB6AFCF1EE4028809.description: Analyze how complex characters (for example: those with multiple or conflicting motivations) develop over the course of a text, interact with other characters, and advance the plot or develop the theme.

605478FD979540D88F0F376CDA3B3506.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

61379F8873D8430B86A46686D265411A.description: Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.

6266748C09C040A89E1923C46B02AE69.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

6406CF5AB145419DB2AD75D24F7F8814.description: Engage and orient the reader by setting out a problem, situation, or observation, establishing multiple points of view, and introducing a narrator and/or characters; create a smooth progression of experiences or events.

6D9BA4D4FFE74F82886E63E314C0395E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

717FAEBDEB4944629737B5D478A5FF6C.description: By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9-10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

728104CD083A49C7B6CEF4E577BCD396.description: Make strategic use of digital media (for example: textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

731D9F59CD5B4CD6BB3698140AE322C0.description: Use precise words and phrases, telling details, and sensory language to convey a vivid picture of the experiences, events, setting, and/or characters.

7952AE31E4754150BEDDE4107385E656.description: Analyze a particular point of view or cultural experience reflected in a work of literature from outside the United States, drawing on a wide reading of world literature.

7B5F6AB976EF432A8CA331B20DF0588C.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9–10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

7D4989420F2B4EF98CB482F6CED893F5.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (for example: dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

802A43FD58204ADC93C77D524BD3C7CF.description: Interpret figures of speech (for example: euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

802CAC8C8C78413AA5C354BC89073260.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

81740279A6134CF594D1A25963481FA7.description: Use a recursive writing process to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing projects.

82F53909E04242A593ED4C896E657F65.description: By the end of grade 9, read and comprehend literature, including stories, dramas, and poems, in the grades 9-10 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

8B04245779F945ED8D7F74A06D22182E.description: Understand the logical progression of ideas in increasingly complex texts.

8B550D98A2B5447D973D6F05A5C905E9.description: Use narrative techniques, such as dialogue, pacing, description, reflection, and multiple plot lines, to develop experiences, events, and/or characters.

8BFB60E9D77446C0AC132B41A4FEAF4C.description: Determine purpose for writing and use rhetorical appeals (i.e., ethos, pathos, logos) to address audience expectations and needs.

8C1351BD3B5D442A9FC900C62136E426.description: Analyze how the author unfolds an analysis or series of ideas or events, including the order in which the points are made, how they are introduced and developed, and the connections that are drawn between them.

97DD437530C34224839B88BAC50DA283.description: Use appropriate and varied transitions to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify the relationships among complex ideas and concepts.

9D7A04BE9E30443EB7A5398EA00CBD1E.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

A33705A654924F43883D61528F475FE5.description: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.

AE7EA52E43CA48CDBAEB24C2635FBBE7.description: Write informative/explanatory texts using complex ideas and organizational structures and features that are useful to audience comprehension.

AF9D14B0EE3349E2AA9D562FCCCBE138.description: Analyze how an author's choices concerning how to structure a text, order events within it (for example: parallel plots), and manipulate time (for example: pacing, flashbacks) create such effects as mystery, tension, or surprise.

B1A5BB70CD3E4EEF91029972296BA2B6.description: Provide a conclusion that follows from and reflects on what is experienced, observed, or resolved over the course of the narrative.

B82A4FB6B6EA467AA1F5BAFD6EAE897F.description: Organize and develop credible presentations tailored to purpose and audience.

B899D38E77934EADAEE739D98631C88A.description: Develop the topic with well-chosen, relevant, and sufficient facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, or other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.

C33DFC100D7F419CBFF172230AE5F436.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of Standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

C6CE7947AE1F436E9A540F873EBC71AB.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

C76C8A00ED7641EAB90D3B6F3D536DA0.description: Use Integration of Knowledge and Ideas to:

CAD3A238062045569BA194F61D680EC3.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

CAF87F5C4A6447868AC592401D3EC5CA.description: Use a range of stylistic devices (for example: poetic techniques, figurative language, imagery, graphic elements) to support the presentation of implicit or explicit themes or to engage and entertain the intended audience.

D3500C934C774D86A84A7EFAAC21978E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

D4EE30E2B87946A2839AA7BD39F87DEF.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

D5C47C88B74C4E5B864C0ABDEF500ACA.description: Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning.

D625288A6E5D47A0BB069BFF15F510AF.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

D6DBEF8E567F4E8E85C2FDBB8164D844.description: Analyze the representation of a subject or a key scene in two different artistic mediums, including what is emphasized or absent in each treatment (for example: Auden's "Musée des Beaux Arts" and Breughel's Landscape with the Fall of Icarus).

D7127603988D43EDB4C6436DABADDB25.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

DB4441A1D266452E90D170D31F6FAC69.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

DBFBE9F22BA94C78AE7EAA0F6B6B3F2F.description: Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims, and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

E1348D19971D49978648D3D29EBA57B9.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (for example: analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

E18DD4BE3A95452A842FD9867EFC4310.description: Use context (for example: the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

E74187F509084541A12860C363FCB1C6.description: Analyze the influence of literary and/or historical context on a text and evaluate the contribution to society made by works of literature that deal with similar topics and themes.

ECDBFC243D144B3C9EBE09000A20F9C0.description: By the end of grade 10, analyze seminal U.S. and world documents of historical and literary significance (for example: the Magna Carta, Machiavelli's The Prince, Washington's Farewell Address, the Gettysburg Address, Roosevelt's Four Freedoms speech, King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail"), including how they influence and address related themes and concepts over the course of time.

F0AB72CDA4F64D7DA15E7FB98CAF80A1.description: Apply grades 9-10 Reading standards to literary nonfiction (for example: "Delineate and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, assessing whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient; identify false statements and fallacious reasoning").

F1C75DF92D6B4EC092D2291FCC06AA06.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

F4F6B81D139C4022A712433EB11389D2.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (for example: by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

F5AF6E80A1DD4E92A1D4AAB9C21E34E9.description: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details; provide an objective summary of the text.

F85BFA673394414A81DBBE66CC4AE0FE.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

F9E09EA8F6C14323B770D7C733F4E12C.description: Use Range of Reading and Complexity of Text to:

FCA371F729754B7B8AF00E94F742A634.description: Respond to others' ideas, and evaluate perspective and rhetoric.
